explanation: The second column v must satisfy (A-2I)v≠0 and (A-2I)^2v=0. Here (A-2I)y=x≠0 and (A-2I)x=0, so y qualifies. Both x and z are already eigenvectors, since (A-2I)x=(A-2I)z=0, and cannot occupy the second position in this Jordan chain. The matrix P=[x,y,z] is invertible and satisfies AP=PJ.
